meta_description: Cytir is an open-source web search index built for AI agents. Download it, run it on your own ground, extend it with your own sources.
og_title: Cytir — the web is our common land
og_description: An open-source web search index built for AI agents. 100 million pages today, one billion as the target, small enough to download in a day.
hero_lead: Cytir is Welsh for common land: ground that belongs to everyone who works it. We are building a web search index that way. It is made for AI agents. Download it, run it on your own ground, extend it with your own sources. What you search stays with you.
fact1_text: pages, in the index you can download today
fact2_text: pages, the target for the full index
fact3_text: for the full index on disk
why_h2: Web search was built for people. Agents need their own.
why_lead: For decades web search has belonged to a handful of companies indexing hundreds of billions of pages. An open alternative at that scale was never realistic: the infrastructure cost is enormous, and the index would be far too large to share. So we asked what an agent actually needs.
why1_p: An agent answering a legal question has to read the exact statutory text before it answers. It needs the authoritative source itself, not a page about it.
why2_p: A model is trained on data that is months old by the time it ships. Search is how an agent sees what changed since.
why3_p: Open-weight models make sovereign LLMs possible. An agent that still sends every query outside your perimeter is only half sovereign.
why4_h: Yours to keep and to change
why4_p: The code and the index are open. A foundation keeps the core index honest, and anyone can run it, fork it or add their own sources.
how_h2: Agents don't need the web the way people do.
how_lead: Two differences let us redesign the index from scratch, for size and for sharing.
how1_h: The model already carries a compressed web
how1_p: So the index only has to fill in what the model lacks: the exact text, the current state, the authoritative URL.
how2_h: A good entry point is enough
how2_p: Agents don't need the perfect page in the top three results. Given a good entry point, they walk the site themselves and find the best page in seconds.
sizes_lead: The same software runs every size. The index lives on NVMe; RAM buys speed, not feasibility. At the full size, private, sovereign web search becomes practical for a team, a company or a country.
size1_runs: a Hetzner server, about 30 € a month
size2_runs: a Hetzner auction server, about 130 € a month
size3_runs: one server; the whole index downloads in under a day
sizes_aside: Medium and full are the next milestones. Small is here now.
mcp_lead: The first version of the index, with 100 million pages, together with the source code to deploy it and to extend it with your own content. A hosted demo is live at websear.ch and connects to any agent via MCP.
mcp_p1: Add the hosted endpoint to your MCP client. The agent gets one tool, search, which returns the URL of the authoritative source with the minimum context needed to choose.
mcp_p2: Your own deployment exposes the same endpoint on your own host.
who_lead: Cytir is a collaboration between impactIA, a Geneva-based foundation, and Vector8, a European AI consultancy. Code and index ship under Apache-2.0.
who_impactia: impactIA governs the open-source community and the contents of the core index. The foundation is based in Geneva.
who_vector8: Vector8 contributes resources to the community and offers deployment and customisation services for enterprises. Offices in Zurich, London, Paris, Skopje and Pristina.
